question: When Emilys' father dies, who becomes her guardian?
final_answer: When Emily’s father dies, she is made the ward of **her only female relation—her aunt, Madame Cheron** (“I have thought it proper to consign you to her care … in my will, till you are of age”).

question: How does Chuck end up on an island?
gold: His plane crashes and his life raft washes up on an island.
final_answer: Chuck ends up on the island because the FedEx cargo plane he’s on plummets out of the sky and crashes into the Pacific during a storm. In the wreck, his life jacket is inflated and he survives in the water as the plane sinks; afterward he’s carried by the waves and washes up on a beach (found face-down/partly buried in the sand), which is the island.

gold: Because he is not sure if he can repay it
final_answer: Tellheim refuses to use Werner’s money because he will not accept it as a loan—he insists he “will not be [Werner’s] debtor,” and says Werner is tormenting him by pressing it on him.

question: Why does Tellheim refuse to engage Minna von Barnhelm at first?
final_answer: Tellheim refuses at first because he believes he is no longer the “former” Tellheim Minna knew—he is now “the discharged, the suspected, the cripple, the beggar”—and therefore feels unworthy to bind her to him. He also insists he will “never…cause you to commit an imprudent [action],” i.e., he will not let Minna sacrifice herself by marrying him in his ruined, dishonoured condition.

trajectory.final_answer: Tellheim refuses at first because he believes he is no longer the “former” Tellheim Minna knew—he is now “the discharged, the suspected, the cripple, the beggar”—and therefore feels unworthy to bind her to him. He also insists he will “never…cause you to commit an imprudent [action],” i.e., he will not let Minna sacrifice herself by marrying him in his ruined, dishonoured condition.

question: What is the legendary Hollow Needle supposed to contain?
gold: It is believed to contain all of the fortunes of the kings of France.
final_answer: The legendary Hollow Needle is supposed to contain the amassed royal treasure of the Kings of France: heaps of gold coins (old Merovingian gold sous, crown-pieces, doubloons, ducats, florins, guineas) along with precious stones and diamonds, and “all the jewels and all the ornaments.”
